Channel: alert-runtime-monitoring  •  bug-type guess: env  •  alerts in group: 1

*Suggested next action:* monitor — file a defect for ms-account-api DB-connection-open failures if frequency climbs. Not a page.

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-21-gateway-microservices-timeout`
Occurrence #60 overall → every-10th *resurface* (≈55 in the last 7 days). Status: *needs-ops-decision*.

ms-gateway-api Ocelot timeouts proxying to `microservices.methodlocal.int`. Confirmed *chronic* this window: gateway `Ocelot.Responder.Middleware` `RequestTimedOutError` Warnings = 82 (12:35–12:45Z) vs 104 24h-ago (−21%, *below* baseline → steady-state, not a regression). Monitor 77419271 last fired 12:43:11Z (−1s to the satellite alert).

Playbook: 1) confirm chronic baseline (done: −21%) → no new incident. 2) aggregate Ocelot timeouts by RequestPath. 3) *check `ki-dns-microservices-method-int-pps-quota` first* (DNS bursts present as Ocelot timeouts). 4) identify slow downstream microservice via `ocelot.*.json`. 5) fix decision tree: raise per-route Ocelot timeout / scale microservices IIS pool / profile upstream (sync-util, preferences, account).
Open Jira: none

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 5)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: data/env  •  alerts in group: 1 (+2 sibling groups, same incident)

Symptoms:
  - runtime-core-api 5XX monitor *70171778* tripped (>30 5XX in 5m by service, 13:08:38Z). runtime-core-api was the dominant service in DD APM 5XX-by-service (~25 of ~36 across all services, 12:55–13:13Z).
  - ES runtime-core-api Errors = 53 vs 33 24h-ago (+60%, modest absolute). Dominated by chronic `Expiring session token failed` ×36 and `Bad count filter on ribbonId` ×11; only a handful of real 5XX: `Redis operation cancelled` ×3, SQL concurrent-access/connection ×1, `EstimateLine` field-delete rolled back (db `gandbsheds`) ×1, `operation was canceled` ×1.
  - Accounts spread, no concentration: appenninofoodusa, tristateelevator2, excelpoolservice, gandbsheds, carlsondockandbarge. All unresolvable for user-count (prod3–5 clusters unconfigured — chronic gap).

Trace IDs: none surfaced (RequestId not populated in runtime error docs)
Likely cause: *transient* — mostly chronic session-token 500s tipping the 5XX monitor just over 30, plus a few transient SQL/Redis cancellations. No deploy (runtime-core unchanged since 2026-05-06). NOT `ki-2026-05-24` RTC-p95 (that's latency-only, zero-error) and NOT `ki-2026-05-21` (frontend/gateway).
Suggested next action: *monitor* (likely transient). If `Bad count filter on ribbonId` recurs across cycles, file a defect on the runtime grid count-filter path.

Cross-channel: the same elevation also surfaced as error-tracking new-issues on #alert-system (`8ccc3dd3`, 13:04Z) and #alert-runtime-monitoring (`86ec52c4`, 13:07Z) — consolidated into this one DM (those two suppressed to actionable).

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 6)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: env / infra (host hang)  •  alerts in group: 33

Symptoms:
  - Centreon infra-check cascade in #alert-system: 33 alerts 13:55:21–14:05:41Z (block-only, no text).
  - Ops already engaged — Ismael Sagullo posted *"rebooting prod-rt-04. server is hung"* at 13:58Z.
  - Coincident runtime-core-api error elevation: 54 vs 6 baseline (~9×) concentrated on host `ip-172-31-194-83` — "Redis operation cancelled" (Runtime.Caching.CacheContext) ×24, cache.clear T-FAULT ×11, a repeating stuck trace.
  - RTC Screen Load p95 monitor 115456700 fired 14:05:20Z (runtime slow — reduced capacity while a node is down; overlaps ki-24).

Trace IDs: 6a0dad3e000000004bad5e816ef5979d
Likely cause: a runtime/agent host (prod-rt-04, which co-hosts runtime-core agents + ms-authentication-api) hung ~13:55Z → Centreon cascade + runtime-core Redis-cancel elevation + brief RTC p95 spike. Not a deploy (runtime-core unchanged since 2026-05-06). Caveat: the hung host isn't directly identifiable in ES (a hung host stops logging; `ip-172-31-194-83` is still emitting, so it's likely NOT prod-rt-04 itself — just where the secondary Redis-cancel errors landed).
Suggested next action: monitor ops' reboot of prod-rt-04; confirm the runtime-core Redis-cancel elevation + RTC p95 recover post-reboot. No bot action — ops is mitigating.

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 5)
Channel: alert-system (error-tracking)  •  bug-type guess: code / env (mobile client)  •  alerts in group: 2

Symptoms:
  - NOVEL, accelerating mobile-client error storm: Method iOS app (v2.1.537) — *"Failed to migrate from AsyncStorage to SecureStore: {code: ERR_KEY_CHAIN}"*.
  - Volume today: 0 in 08–11Z → 826 in 11–13Z → ~4859 in the last 20 min (≈240/min) → 5996 total, vs ~3 in the 24h-ago baseline (~80×).
  - Logged via mobilenative.method.me POST /apps/v1/logging/mobile (server is just a relay; spread evenly across PROD-NEW-04/5/6 = ingestion, not a server fault).
  - Surfaced via error-tracking new-issue monitor 227951254 (Alert state). Attribution of the exact Slack posts to this issue is INFERRED — block bodies are unreadable; basis is the ES volume signature + monitor state.

Trace IDs: n/a (client-side; UA Method/2.1.537 CFNetwork/Darwin = iOS)
Likely cause: a recent Method iOS release (observed 2.1.537) added an AsyncStorage→SecureStore migration that fails on the iOS keychain (ERR_KEY_CHAIN) — likely a missing/incorrect keychain access group/entitlement or a SecureStore key collision. Each affected launch retries + logs → the accelerating volume. No server-side fix.
Suggested next action: file a defect / route to the mobile team for v2.1.537 (wrap the migration in try/catch + fall back to AsyncStorage; fix the keychain entitlement). Optionally down-rank /apps/v1/logging/mobile client errors below ERROR to cut error-tracking noise.
